inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 397.7M shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q EPS note) plus ~0.9M dilutive effect (Q3 weighted diluted 399.8 less weighted basic 398.9). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: equity-based compensation add-back 169 plus 51 of cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement (financing activities). WM publishes no combined figure (no adjusted-EBITDA SBC line), so the two lines are summed. 9M-2026: 139 + 40.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rates. Cost of equity ~8.3% (10-year US Treasury ~4.3% assumed, not fetched in this run + beta floored at 0.8 x 5% ERP; WM's observed beta is nearer 0.6-0.7). After-tax cost of debt ~3.9% (senior notes ~5% pre-tax). Weights ~81% equity / 19% debt at market. That computes to ~7.4-7.5%; 7.5% used in all three scenarios -- risk is carried by the scenario weights, not by per-scenario discount rates. Post-Stericycle leverage (~2.9x net debt / trailing EBITDA, down from ~3.6x at close) is reflected in the debt weight, not an extra premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost sits inside operating expenses and so inside EBITDA; operating lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. Finance leases are inside reported total debt. One treatment, charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests are immaterial (1 on the balance sheet, ~1 of annual income); no adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon, three scenarios. Routing: WM is a US operating company (collection, transfer, landfill, recycling, landfill-gas energy, regulated medical waste) whose value is a stream of free cash flow -- not a bank, REIT, holdco or deal situation -- so the owner-FCF row of the dcf-methods table applies. First valuation of this ticker; no prior model. | FLOW BASIS: the engine's flows are UNLEVERED (tax on EBIT, no interest deducted) and net debt comes off at the end. last_fcf / reported_fcf are the levered historical figures (OCF - capex, before WM's own add-back of divestiture proceeds: WM's non-GAAP FCF was 2,937 in FY2025 vs 2,816 here; asset-sale proceeds are not a recurring operating flow so the lower figure is used). Year-1 cross-check: trailing-twelve-month OCF - capex 3,740, less SBC and equity taxes ~220, plus after-tax interest ~735 = ~4,250 unlevered owner FCF, against the base case's year-1 build of ~4.2B. | EBITDA MARGIN BASIS: income from operations + depreciation, depletion, amortisation and accretion, plus SBC (charged on its own line), LESS ~0.75pp of revenue for cash landfill capping/closure/post-closure and remediation settlements (~210/yr), which are real cash costs that the accretion add-back would otherwise hide. 9M-2026 on that basis is ~30.0%. This is why landfill and environmental liabilities (~3.3B) are NOT deducted in the bridge -- they are charged in the flows. | BUYBACKS: 1,583 in 9M-2026 after a pause through FY2025 to delever from Stericycle; the flat count is being funded. | NOT INCLUDED: investments in unconsolidated entities (711, largely tax-credit structures whose benefit is in the low early cash-tax rate) are not added to the bridge. | INTEREST INCOME: not stripped -- WM is a net borrower. | ANALYSIS JSON: WM_Analysis.json did not exist when this was built; scenario axes are drawn from the 10-K/10-Q MD&A and the kpis table (yield, volume, segment revenue). Re-check the narratives against it when it lands. | 10-year Treasury yield was assumed, not fetched.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (~6%) diverges >30% from revenue 5yr (~10.6%) and EPS 5yr (~13.7%). Revenue CAGRs are inflated by the Nov-2024 Stericycle acquisition (~$2.5B of FY2025 revenue) and 2021-22 inflation-era yield; EPS by buybacks and a COVID-depressed FY2020 base. Forward paths are built from organic drivers (collection & disposal yield ~3.5-4%, volume ~0.5%), not from any trailing CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = (OCF - capex) - SBC add-back - cash taxes withheld on equity awards: FY2020 1,643; FY2022 1,826; FY2025 2,596. Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are within ~0.6pp of each other: SBC is under 1% of revenue and is not growing faster than cash flow. FY2022-FY2025 FCF was depressed by ~$3B of sustainability growth capex (recycling automation, RNG plants) that is now rolling off; 9M-2026 OCF-capex was 2,930 vs 2,006 in 9M-2025.

base.narrative: Year 1 is FY2026, set from nine months of actuals (revenue 19,757, income from operations 3,645, D&A 2,304, capex 1,937) plus a Q4 in line with Q3. Thereafter collection and disposal yield settles at 3.5-4% (it has decelerated from 6.7% in FY2022 to 3.4% in Q3-2026), volume adds ~0.5%, and the completed recycling-automation and landfill-gas plants add a point of growth in FY2027-28 before fading. Margin rises ~2.5pp over the decade from Stericycle cost synergies (already visible in SG&A at 9.6% of revenue vs 10.3%), the high-margin Renewable Energy segment scaling, and continued price-over-cost spread. Capex normalises near 10.5% of revenue as sustainability growth spend ends; cash tax ramps from ~17% (RNG investment tax credits, bonus depreciation) to 24%. Acquisitions beyond what is already owned are not modelled, on either the revenue or the cash side.

bull.narrative: Pricing discipline holds across the industry so yield stays above 4% while cost inflation cools, Healthcare Solutions is fully cross-sold into WM's commercial base and reaches solid-waste-like margins, and RIN and recycled-commodity prices are supportive so the ~$3B sustainability build earns its underwritten returns. Margin reaches the mid-34s (engine basis) and capital intensity drops to ~10.2% as the fleet and landfill-gas build are behind it. Needs three things at once: price, healthcare integration, and commodity/RIN prices.

bear.narrative: Yield decays to CPI as inflation-linked contracts reset and competitors chase volume; industrial and construction-and-demolition volumes fall in a downturn; Healthcare Solutions keeps losing customers after the Stericycle billing/ERP disruption; RIN prices stay weak after policy changes so Renewable Energy under-earns on its invested capital. Margin stalls just under 30%, capex stays at 11% (landfill cell construction and fleet do not flex), and the market pays a lower 16x terminal multiple for a 2.5%-growth utility-like stream. No solvency issue: leverage is investment grade throughout.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): yield has decelerated every year since FY2022, Healthcare Solutions revenue is flat year on year at ~640/quarter two years after acquisition, and leverage is still above the pre-deal level. Base 50%: the business is contractual, price-led and has compounded through every cycle in the data. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs sustained above-CPI pricing, a healthcare turnaround and supportive RIN/commodity prices together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: WM is a price-led, landfill-anchored compounder valued on unlevered owner free cash flow. The valuation question is not survival but how much of the sustainability capex roll-off and Stericycle synergy is already in a price near 28x enterprise value to year-1 unlevered owner FCF. The terminal multiple cap (20x) binds in base and bull, so value is driven by the year-10 margin and capital intensity far more than by the growth path.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal-value dependence: most of enterprise value sits in the terminal year, and the 20x cap binds; one turn of exit multiple moves base value by several percent.
Capital intensity: each 0.5pp of revenue on capex is ~130-200 of annual FCF, capitalised at 20x.
Yield durability: collection and disposal yield has fallen from 6.7% (FY2022) to 3.4% (Q3-2026); the base case assumes it stabilises at 3.5-4%.
Healthcare Solutions: flat revenue since acquisition; synergy is showing in SG&A but not in growth.
Renewable Energy earnings depend on RIN prices and on 45Z/Section 48 credits, both policy-set.
Cash tax: the low current rate rests on investment tax credits and bonus depreciation; the model ramps to 24%.
Discount rate assumed from an un-fetched Treasury yield; see the required-return table.
